rounds.text: Tinna Rubber & Infrastructure Ltd currently trades at a significant premium to its sector, with a P/E of 31.12x compared to the benchmark of 23.17x and a P/B of 6.39x against the sector’s 2.63x [E6, E7]. This aggressive valuation is further underscored by an EV/EBITDA of 18.29x, which sits well above the sector benchmark of 14.07x [E11]. While the company has shown recent profit growth, long-term sales performance remains stagnant with a 10-year compounded sales growth of 0% [E14]. Furthermore, the company is currently burning cash, reporting a negative free cash flow of Rs -49 Cr in March 2026 [E36]. Institutional confidence appears to be waning, as evidenced by negative money flow and a reduction in promoter holdings from 73.81% to 67.21% since September 2023 [E42, E45]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong 5-year profit growth of 238% and maintains a solid return on equity [E19, E61].

evidence.quote: However, we are seeing very robust growth in our industrial sector. That is driven by, due to these crisis, the benefit that we have seen is there is higher motivation for blending of rubber in bitumen as well as for use of recycled rubber materials in new products.

evidence.fact: EBITDA margins for Q1 FY27 exceeded 21%.
evidence.quote: During the quarter, we achieved record financial performance with EBITDA exceeding INR30 crores, PAT surpassing INR20 crores, EBITDA margins of over 21% and PAT margins of more than 13% on both stand-alone and consolidated basis.

evidence.quote: FY26 was another year of strong execution for Tinna Rubber, despite geopolitical uncertainties and a dynamic operating environment, we achieved record tire processing volumes and delivered robust EBITDA margins of over 17%.
